planets.name: Mercury
mission_visits: Mariner 10 — NASA, 1974–75 (first spacecraft to visit Mercury; three flybys mapped ≈ 45 % of the surface)
MESSENGER — NASA, 2011–15 (first orbiter; complete surface map, gravity field, magnetic field, ice in polar craters)
BepiColombo — ESA / JAXA, 2018 launch · Mercury orbit insertion late 2026 (dual orbiter: MPO + Mio)

planets.name: Venus
mission_visits: Venera 1–16 — USSR, 1961–83 (sustained Venus campaign; Venera 7 first soft-landing on another planet 1970; Venera 9 first surface images 1975)
Mariner 2 — NASA, 1962 (first successful interplanetary flyby of any planet)
Mariner 5 / 10 — NASA, 1967 / 1974 (atmosphere, gravity, UV imaging)
Pioneer Venus 1 + 2 — NASA, 1978 (orbiter + multi-probe atmospheric descent)
Vega 1 + 2 — USSR, 1985 (lander + balloon, en route to Halley)
Magellan — NASA, 1990–94 (radar mapping of 98 % of the surface)
Venus Express — ESA, 2006–14 (polar orbit; super-rotation, lightning, atmospheric escape)
Akatsuki — JAXA, 2015– (equatorial cloud dynamics, currently active)
Parker Solar Probe + BepiColombo — multiple gravity-assist flybys (2020s)

planets.name: Earth
mission_visits: Apollo 8, 10, 11–17 — NASA, 1968–72 (Earthrise; first human views of the full disk from cislunar space)
International Space Station — multinational, 2000– (continuous human presence in LEO)
Landsat 1–9 — NASA / USGS, 1972– (longest-running Earth-observation programme)
GOES, Meteosat, Himawari, Elektro-L — geostationary weather constellations
Sentinel 1–6 — ESA Copernicus, 2014– (radar + multi-spectral + ocean altimetry)
Aqua / Terra / MODIS — NASA, 1999–2002– (climate + land + ocean spectroscopy)
DSCOVR / EPIC — NASA / NOAA, 2015– (sunward L1 view; full-disk Earth every two hours)

planets.name: Mars
mission_visits: Mariner 4 / 6 / 7 / 9 — NASA, 1965–72 (first flybys then first Mars orbiter, global mapping)
Viking 1 + 2 — NASA, 1976 (first successful Mars landings; biology experiments)
Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner — NASA, 1997 (first wheeled rover on another planet)
Mars Global Surveyor + Odyssey + Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter — NASA, 1997– (multi-decade orbital coverage; MRO HiRise)
Mars Express + ExoMars TGO — ESA, 2003– / 2016– (mineralogy, methane search)
Spirit + Opportunity — NASA, 2004 (twin rovers; Opportunity lasted 14 years)
Phoenix — NASA, 2008 (north polar lander; first to touch water ice)
Curiosity / MSL — NASA, 2012– (Gale crater; nuclear-powered rover, still operating)
MAVEN — NASA, 2014– (atmospheric escape physics)
Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) — ISRO, 2014–22 (India's first interplanetary mission)
InSight — NASA, 2018–22 (first interior-structure mission; marsquakes)
Hope (Al Amal) — UAE, 2021– (atmospheric weather monitoring)
Tianwen-1 + Zhurong — CNSA, 2021 (China's first orbital + rover combination)
Perseverance + Ingenuity — NASA, 2021– (Jezero crater; first powered flight on another planet)
ExoMars Rosalind Franklin — ESA, scheduled 2028 launch

planets.name: Jupiter
mission_visits: Pioneer 10 + 11 — NASA, 1973 / 1974 (first flybys; first close-up images)
Voyager 1 + 2 — NASA, 1979 (volcanism on Io, ring discovery, fine atmospheric detail)
Galileo — NASA, 1995–2003 (first Jupiter orbiter; atmospheric entry probe; Europa + Ganymede + Callisto + Io detail)
Cassini-Huygens — NASA / ESA / ASI, 2000 (gravity-assist flyby, joint imaging campaign with Galileo)
New Horizons — NASA, 2007 (gravity-assist flyby en route to Pluto; high-res Io and Europa)
Juno — NASA, 2016– (polar orbiter; magnetic field, JunoCam, deep atmospheric structure)
Europa Clipper — NASA, 2024– (en route to Jovian system; Europa close flybys from 2030)
JUICE — ESA, 2023– (en route; orbital insertion at Ganymede in 2034)

planets.name: Saturn
mission_visits: Pioneer 11 — NASA, 1979 (first Saturn flyby; ring detail and Titan distant view)
Voyager 1 + 2 — NASA, 1980 / 1981 (close flybys; ring structure, Titan haze, F-ring shepherding)
Cassini-Huygens — NASA / ESA / ASI, 2004–17 (13-year orbiter; Huygens probe landed on Titan in 2005; Grand Finale ring-crossings)

planets.name: Uranus
mission_visits: Voyager 2 — NASA, 24 January 1986 flyby (only spacecraft to visit; imaged Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel, Titania, Oberon; ring + magnetosphere data)

planets.name: Neptune
mission_visits: Voyager 2 — NASA, 25 August 1989 flyby (only spacecraft to visit; Great Dark Spot, Triton flyby, ring confirmation)

planets.name: Pluto
mission_visits: New Horizons — NASA, 14 July 2015 flyby (only spacecraft to visit; close-up imaging of Sputnik Planitia, Charon, atmospheric structure)
